- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- If model shows sharp upward spike after a recent dip, true outcome often overshoots and then corrects — cap forecast peak at 1.2x recent 7-day average.
- In high-sentiment volatility periods (e.g., sentiment swings > ±0.3), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast with 7-day moving average to reduce false peaks.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often underestimates continuation — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.2 and price > 70.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 3–5 days (especially after spikes), model is overreacting — delay forecast peak by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 5–8%.
- In low-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment < -0.2 for 5+ days), model tends to underestimate downward risk — add 3–5% downward buffer to forecast if sentiment remains negative.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day mean and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overestimating momentum.
